assertions.text: Package options (fragile, insuredValue, handling) are collapsed into a single map column like [fragile: true, insuredValue: 500] — not kept as three separate columns with mostly-blank cells. Rows with no options use a blank cell or [:].
assertions.evidence: Options appear as three separate columns: 'Fragile | Insured Value | Handling'. Not collapsed into map syntax like [fragile: true, insuredValue: 500].

assertions.text: A @TypeConverter method is present that accepts Map<String, String> (or similar) and returns PackageOptions, applying defaults for missing keys.
assertions.evidence: No @TypeConverter method is present. Code manually constructs PackageOptions with if-statements: 'if (fragile) opts.setFragile(true)'.

assertions.text: Dimensions are represented as a [L, W, H] list in the table — not as three separate length/width/height columns
assertions.evidence: Dimensions appear as three separate columns: 'Length | Width | Height'. Not collapsed into [L, W, H] list syntax.

assertions.text: At least one table uses value set syntax {DHL, UPS, FEDEX} (or subset) to express carrier equivalence, rather than duplicating rows per carrier
Multiple @TableTest methods exist, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing base rates, surcharges, dimensional weight, and carrier equivalence
assertions.evidence: Two @TableTest methods: 'shippingCost' for physical attributes and 'packageOptionSurcharges' for declared options surcharges.

assertions.text: Weight and cost parameters use BigDecimal (not double or String). Dimensions use Integer or int.
assertions.evidence: Weight and cost use 'double': 'double weight' and 'double expectedCost'. Should be BigDecimal. Dimensions correctly use 'int'.

assertions.text: Each table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
Scenario names describe conditions ('EU express, light package', 'Oversized with fragile') — not outcomes ('8.00', 'Surcharge applied') or generic labels ('Test 1').
assertions.evidence: Scenario names describe conditions: 'EU express light', 'Dimensional weight overrides', 'Fragile and insured'. Not outcomes or generic labels.

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Cost?', 'Base rate?')
Column names use domain language ('Zone', 'Weight (kg)', 'Dimensions', 'Options', 'Cost?') — not code identifiers ('shippingZone', 'weightKg', 'dims')
assertions.evidence: First table uses code identifiers: 'Region', 'Speed', 'Weight', 'Length', 'Width', 'Height', 'Carrier' instead of collapsed 'Dimensions' or 'Options' or 'Zone'.

assertions.text: Test method bodies contain no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: if statement found in method body

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
Each test method has a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: @Description annotations provide clear titles: 'Dimensional weight = length × width × height / 5000...' and 'All rows: EU standard zone, 3.0 kg...'

assertions.text: Output contains no Groovy or Spock syntax: no def, where:, expect:, given:, GString interpolation (#variable), Spock assertions (thrown(), old()), or Groovy list literals ([] as Set).
